raw_response:
Alright, let me think through this year's plan. I'm 55, been on these 3.8 mu for 30 years, and it's just me and my wife now — our son works in Handan, comes home for Spring Festival. So whatever I do, the two of us have to be able to handle it ourselves, with some help from the village machinery.

**Wheat first** — it's already in the ground. I planted Shimai 15 around October 5th last fall, about 25 jin per mu of seed. Before planting I spread 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer (15-15-15), plus about 10 kg of urea, and had the tractor guy rotary-till it in. Standard way, same as everybody around here.

Now it's spring, so what I need to plan is the topdress and the irrigation schedule. The extension fellow at the station said 15 kg of N per mu total is plenty, but I've seen what happens when you cut back too much — the wheat comes up thin and the ears are small. So when it greens up in early March I'll put down about 12 kg of urea per mu, then run the first irrigation right after so it washes in. The well is shared with three other households, costs about 40 yuan per mu each time we pump. I'll do three irrigations — returning-green, jointing, and grain-filling. Some neighbors do four, but that's another 150 yuan out the door on my little plot, and I'd rather keep that money for maize inputs.

Weeds I'll spray once with a 2,4-D type mix before jointing, maybe 15 yuan per mu. If I see aphids at heading I'll spray once more. I don't spray "just in case" — my father never did and I don't either.

I'm expecting around 430 kg per mu, same as last year. The combine comes through around June 8th — hired, 60 yuan per mu. That's cheaper than the three days of back-breaking work it'd take the two of us by hand, and at my age my back can't do it anyway.

**Then maize, right after wheat.** The turnaround is tight — maybe 5 days. I hire the village direct-seeder at 30 yuan per mu; it goes through and plants straight into the wheat stubble, no tilling. Saves time and the straw holds moisture. I plant Zhengdan 958 — everyone around here plants it because it's reliable and the buyers know it. Seed is about 50 yuan per mu.

For maize I put 30 kg per mu of compound with the seed, then at the big-flare stage (about 6-8 leaves, usually mid-July) I topdress 20 kg of urea per mu. That's my habit — get most of the N in at the right time when the plant is growing fast. Pre-emergence herbicide right after planting, about 20 yuan per mu.

Irrigation for maize I only do if it's dry — usually the July-August rains are enough. Plan for one irrigation, but we'll see. Yield should be around 480 kg per mu.

In October the corn harvester comes through — 80 yuan per mu. Then we clean up and start the wheat cycle again.

Money-wise, the whole year runs me about 3,000 yuan on inputs and hired machinery across the 3.8 mu. Tight, but we manage. Most of what comes off the land we sell — we only keep maybe 100 kg of wheat for flour and a bit of maize for the chickens.
